messages:
maria-ml: Heads-up: ACME Finance wants a customer-specific instruct variant for their compliance pipeline — 64k context, prefer int8/ptq, must keep hallucination FDR < 0.5% vs our baseline. Request came through solutions; need triage and bring-up plan. cc @priya-ml @alex-platform

alex-platform: Thanks. Do we have model family? Are they asking supervised instruct fine-tune or just instruction prompt templates over a base model?

maria-ml: They want an instruct-tuned variant — policy & style constraints baked in. Preferred base is a 180B-class open model (they referenced an external checkpoint), but open to Llama 3 family if it gives better latency. Also they want retokenization/support for very long legal docs (64k).

priya-ml: Ok. Quick checklist I propose: 1) feasibility: can we run 64k with int8 on Dedicated? 2) eval harness: compliance/regression suites 3) perf: p50/p99 and KV-cache sizing 4) safety & hallucination checks 5) rollout plan + canary. I'll draft PRD and checklist.

sam-sre: On hosting: 64k + int8 -> memory estimate is non-trivial. KV cache and hidden state for 64k will push memory needs very high. Likely need either >192GB vRAM or sharded across 2x80GB A100 with model parallel. NVMe staging for long contexts may be required. Expect cost to spike ~3x.

maria-ml: Good call. Priya — can you add a quant sweep plan? We should include int8, int4 fallback profiles and capture fidelity deltas on our compliance eval. Include response truncation checks.

priya-ml: Will add. Proposed eval targets: hallucination <=0.5% on compliance set; instruction fidelity >=95% on prompt->expected action; latency p50 < 400ms for 2k contexts, p95 < 1.5s for 8k. For 32k-64k we'll relax SLOs. Thoughts?

alex-platform: p95 targets might be optimistic for 64k. Suggest tiered SLOs by context class: up to 8k (fast), 8k-32k (mid), 32k-64k (long). For 32k+ expect p95 multi-second and higher throughput cost.

maria-ml: Agreed. Prioritization: ACME is enterprise but not yet Dedicated — sales says customer will pay for Private deployment. They want a 6-week timeline. Is that realistic?

sam-sre: 6 weeks is tight. Kernel selection + quant experiments ~2 weeks; infra + perf tuning 1.5-2 weeks; Evals + safety review ~1 week. Minimum ~4.5 wks if everything goes well and we don't hit license/legal blockers. Need model-family decision ASAP.

priya-ml: I'll spin up an eval job today comparing Llama3-70B and the open-180B-class base for LoRA instruct-tune on their 50k examples. Will post initial metrics (hallucination, fidelity, token-level deltas).

eval-bot: Job 2026-03-20-013 queued: run/evals/acme-variant/initial_comparison. Estimated runtime ~36h.

maria-ml: :thumbsup: Also note legal wants encryption-at-rest + customer KMS and full audit logs; that'll push them to Private. Keep Security in loop.

alex-platform: Also need to confirm license for chosen base model for redistribution as a customer-specific variant. I'll check with Legal.

priya-ml: For quantization: plan sweep on the shortlist (70B, 180B-class) across dynamic int8, AWQ-int8, NF4-int8 and q4_0/q4_1 int4. Capture KL divergence, instruction-loss delta, and hallucination rate. If int8 hurts fidelity, fall back to int8+fp16 for sensitive layers.

sam-sre: When quant profiles exist, run a throughput/cost simulation using Redwood Optimize to estimate per-token cost and capacity. I'll make a cost-card for Sales.

maria-ml: Decision points we need in the triage matrix: (A) proceed with 70B instruct variant; (B) proceed with 180B-class base instruct variant; (C) decline / suggest alternative due to cost or compliance. Assign owners.

priya-ml: I'll own A vs B evals. Sam will own infra/cost simulation. Alex will own legal/license check. Maria will be customer comms / final decision.

alex-platform: Acknowledged. I'll ping Legal and Security; aiming to have answers by EOD tomorrow.

maria-ml: Thanks. Priya — drop a minimal bring-up checklist into GH under eng-ml and paste link here once done.

priya-ml: Done: https://github.com/redwood/eng-ml/pull/314 — checklist includes feasibility matrix, eval harness template, quant sweep plan, rollout steps, canary gating.

sam-sre: Added infra notes in review: include NVMe swap strategy, per-shard KV cache sizing, and rollback plan to a lower-context variant.

priya-ml: Addressed comments. Also added a small synthetic prompt set for compliance to catch hallucinations early in CI.

eval-bot: Job 2026-03-21-090 completed: initial_comparison. Results: Llama3-70B LoRA -> hallucination 0.62%, fidelity 93.7%; open-180B-class LoRA -> hallucination 0.48%, fidelity 95.1%. Full logs: https://ci.redwood/jobs/2026-03-21-090

maria-ml: Interesting — the 180B-class base looks better on fidelity but is heavier to host. Priya, can you run AWQ-int8 on the 180B-class model and report output delta vs fp16 baseline?

priya-ml: Queued quant sweep (awq-int8, nf4-int8) on open-180B-class. ETA ~48h. Will surface KL and hallucination delta.

alex-platform: :eyes: Also flagging potential attribution/license clause on that open-180B checkpoint. Legal will advise.

sam-sre: If 180B-class int8 delta < 1% hallucination increase and cost <~2x, we can propose Dedicated with 1-month canary and stricter monitoring.

maria-ml: Perfect. Let's reconvene early next week after quant results + legal signoff. Filing this thread into the eng-ml intake tracker.
